headline: Buttigieg allies launch effort to back another presidential run
author: Adam Wren

paragraphs.text: Allies of former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg are launching an independent, grassroots effort urging him to undertake a second presidential campaign ahead of 2028.

Team Pete PAC will be led by Jennifer Holdsworth, the former national campaign manager of Buttigieg’s unsuccessful 2017 bid for DNC chair, and Mohsin Syed, his former chief of staff at the Transportation Department. The PAC is aiming to bring together volunteers and grassroots donors who backed Buttigieg’s 2020 presidential bid.
“Mohsin and I have traveled the country this year, and everywhere we go, people ask us the same question: how can I help Pete?” Holdsworth said in a statement.
Team Pete PAC is independent and has no ties to Buttigieg’s Win the Era PAC, nor is it a presidential committee.
Through Win the Era, Buttigieg campaigned with 102 candidates across the map for the midterms, visiting 38 states (19 of them twice).

Asked on MS NOW’s “Morning Joe” on Wednesday whether he had a timeline to make a decision, Buttigieg said he would be “surprised” if he was the first potential 2028 presidential candidate “to make news” and said he’s “certainly not cooking up anything to announce in the next few weeks.”

Even as it forms to press Buttigieg to mount a second presidential campaign, Team Pete PAC is urging potential backers to take part in community service — a nod to Buttigeig’s proposed national service program he proposed as a candidate.
“I’ve seen up close what Pete can do,” Syed said. “He has a unique ability to bring people together and inspire action.”
